recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片中央三顆大型母細胞聚在一起，核大而圓、染色質細緻，細胞質量中等至豐富、呈灰藍色且無明顯顆粒，符合單核母細胞（monoblast）的外觀；左下另有一顆退化變形的細胞。
features: Cluster of three large blasts, roughly 2-3 times the diameter of adjacent red cells
Round to slightly oval nuclei with finely dispersed, delicate chromatin; nucleoli are indistinct at this focus
Moderate to abundant gray-blue cytoplasm without visible granules or Auer rods
A distorted, degenerating/smudged cell at the lower left
Background of red cells with abundant stain precipitate; photographed through the eyepiece with limited sharpness
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows a small cluster of large circulating blasts in a background of red cells with prominent stain precipitate. The blasts have round to slightly oval nuclei with finely dispersed chromatin and a moderate to abundant amount of agranular gray-blue cytoplasm; no Auer rods are identified. An additional degenerated cell is present at the lower left. Image resolution limits assessment of nucleoli and fine granules, and nonspecific esterase or flow cytometry is required to confirm monocytic lineage. Findings are consistent with circulating monoblasts in acute monoblastic leukemia.

ddx.vs: Myeloblasts have scantier cytoplasm, may show Auer rods and azurophilic granules, and are MPO-strong/NSE-negative, whereas monoblasts have abundant gray-blue cytoplasm and are NSE-positive.
Promonocytes show folded or convoluted nuclei and fine lilac granules, while monoblasts in this field have round nuclei and agranular cytoplasm.
Megakaryoblasts often show cytoplasmic blebs and cluster formation but are CD41/CD61-positive and NSE/lysozyme-negative.
Mature monocytes have condensed, lobulated nuclei and vacuolated gray cytoplasm without fine blast chromatin.
